docs.text: AI4S-Bench contributor guide AI4S-Bench collects research tasks in AI for Science and packages accepted tasks as reproducible Harbor benchmarks. The public task implementations live in the ai4s-benchmark repository . Choose a path Submit a proposal to suggest a research task. Apply to review proposals in your field. Review a proposal after your reviewer application is approved. Contribute a new task after its proposal receives human approval. Run the complete example to see a task layout and verifier. From idea to runnable task A researcher submits the proposal form . The site creates a GitHub Discussion and lists it on the task board . AI review may post a recommendation. It is advice for the community, not an approval decision. An authorized human reviewer publishes a structured review. Reviews remain in the Discussion history; subsequent reviews add new entries. After human approval, a contributor opens a task PR that links to that Discussion. Maintainers check the decision, task files, and runnable result. Maintenance of an existing task can go straight to a repair PR. It does not need a new proposal Discussion.

docs.text: Apply to become a reviewer Researchers with relevant expertise can apply through the reviewer application form . Provide your name, contact email, research areas, affiliation, and a short account of your experience. A GitHub account can be supplied with the application; it is required to publish reviews later. Submit the application and wait for the project team to review it. The application itself does not grant reviewer access. After approval, sign in to AI4S-Bench with the approved GitHub identity and open a proposal from the task board . The project team handles the approval and follow-up through the contact details in your application. Once access is enabled, use the reviewer guide to publish a review.

docs.text: Contribute a new task Submit a new Harbor task only after its proposal receives an approved human review . The proposal guide explains how to create the Discussion. Include that Discussion URL in your PR description. AI review alone is not approval. Build the task Place a task under tasks/<domain>/<field>/<task-slug>/ . The first domain in the proposal is primary and determines <domain> ; the proposal's research field within it determines <field> . See the seven supported domain slugs and metadata rules . Follow that guide and include at least: File Purpose task.toml Harbor task metadata, including [metadata].domain , [metadata].field , and [task].name instruction.md Instructions visible to the agent environment/Dockerfile Reproducible execution environment solution/solve.sh Oracle solution tests/test.sh Verifier that writes /logs/verifier/reward.txt Use an identifier such as ai4sbench/my-task for [task].name . Make shell scripts executable and use LF line endings. The verifier should emit a numeric reward; demonstrate that the Oracle succeeds and a no-op agent does not. See the complete example . For example, a new task in tasks/physics/inverse-problems/my-task/ includes: [metadata] domain = "physics" field = "inverse-problems" The PR check requires these two keys to match the folders for new tasks. Existing task repairs keep their current paths. Validate and open the PR Install the pinned runtime described in bench/README.md , then run Harbor from the repository root: harbor run -p tasks/<domain>/<field>/<task-slug> -a oracle -e docker harbor run -p tasks/<domain>/<field>/<task-slug> -a nop -e docker Open a PR against AI4S-Bench/ai4s-benchmark with a summary of the task, the human-approved proposal Discussion URL , the validation commands, and the observed rewards. CI checks the directory structure and Discussion link format. Maintainers verify the proposal's actual human approval and review the task behavior. If your PR only repairs an existing task, say so in its description. A maintenance PR does not require a new proposal link, but should explain the change and show the relevant validation result.

docs.text: Complete example: AMR Poisson task fixture The repository includes amr-poisson-contribution-example . It is a minimal Harbor contribution fixture : the instruction asks the agent to write a specific marker, and the verifier checks it. It demonstrates the packaging and validation workflow, not a scientific AMR Poisson problem. Its older mathematical-sciences directory is retained for compatibility; new tasks use one of the seven primary-domain folders in CONTRIBUTING.md . Files tasks/mathematical-sciences/applied-mathematics/amr-poisson-contribution-example/ ├── task.toml ├── instruction.md ├── environment/Dockerfile ├── solution/solve.sh └── tests/test.sh task.toml declares [task].name = "ai4sbench/amr-poisson-contribution-example" and records its existing folder names in [metadata].domain and [metadata].field . instruction.md specifies the output. The Dockerfile provides the runtime, solution/solve.sh is the Oracle, and tests/test.sh writes 1 or 0 to /logs/verifier/reward.txt after checking the output. Run it Set up the pinned Harbor runtime as described in bench/README.md . From the benchmark repository root, run: harbor run -p tasks/mathematical-sciences/applied-mathematics/amr-poisson-contribution-example -a oracle -e docker harbor run -p tasks/mathematical-sciences/applied-mathematics/amr-poisson-contribution-example -a nop -e docker The Oracle run should report reward 1.0 ; the no-op run should report 0.0 . This positive and negative check confirms that the verifier discriminates between the intended solution and no solution. Describe your PR For a new task, include the URL of its human-approved GitHub Discussion. Use this outline, replacing the placeholder with the real approved proposal: Summary: Add <task name> with instructions, environment, Oracle, and verifier. Approved proposal: https://github.com/AI4S-Bench/ai4s-benchmark/discussions/<number> Validation: harbor run -p <task path> -a oracle -e docker → reward 1.0 harbor run -p <task path> -a nop -e docker → reward 0.0 The PR that repaired this fixture is a maintenance example. An existing-task repair does not need a new proposal Discussion. It cannot stand in for a newly approved research task.

docs.text: Review a proposal Only approved reviewers can publish a human review. First apply for reviewer access , then sign in with your approved GitHub identity. Open the task board and select a proposal. Read the proposal, its Discussion, prior human reviews, and any AI recommendation. Check scientific value, feasibility, reproducibility, and whether the proposed outcome can be evaluated. In the reviewer workbench on the task detail page, choose Approved , Changes requested , or Rejected . Fill in the structured assessment and actionable comments. Preview your review and publish it. The site adds a new review reply to the GitHub Discussion and keeps it in the review history. A later review adds another entry rather than replacing the earlier one. AI review is advisory and does not change the human decision. A contributor may open a PR for a new task only after human approval. For that handoff, share the approved Discussion URL and the task guide .

docs.text: Submit a proposal Use a proposal to describe a research task before implementing it as a new benchmark. Start at the proposal form . Sign in with GitHub when the site asks you to. Describe the scientific area, task objective, available inputs, expected output, and how an answer could be checked. Include data access and reproducibility details where relevant. The form offers Materials Science, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, AI / ML, Applied Mathematics, and Interdisciplinary. If you select several, put the primary domain first; the research field belongs to that domain. Submit the form. The site creates a GitHub Discussion for the proposal and displays it on the task board . Follow the Discussion for questions and reviews. Use the task page to make edits or provide clarifications requested by reviewers. The AI review is a recommendation. Wait for an authorized human reviewer to approve the proposal before opening a PR for a new task. Keep the Discussion URL: your task PR must link to it. Read Contribute a new task for the implementation process.
